# spec/pr/mutate

`spec/pr/mutate` — the mutants of a module's changed lines, and the
verdict on how the test met them. A mutant changes one operator, one
literal or one statement on a line the change added since the base,
inside a declaration the contract's functions reach (`spec/pr/scope`); the
test must kill every one that builds, unless the contract allows a
survivor on that line with a reason. The gate also fails when there is
nothing to mutate, when no mutant builds, and when the test fails on the
unmutated module, since then it proves nothing, and when too many builds
or test runs pass their time limit, since a timeout is neither a kill nor a
survival. Running the mutants is
`spec/pr/mutaterun`'s, and so is mutateCheck, which joins them.

Generated from [src/spec/pr/mutate.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/pr/mutate.ts).

### MUTATE_KILLED

The test failed on the mutant: it pins the line down.

### MUTATE_SURVIVED

The test passed on the mutant: behaviour no requirement pins down.


<a id="mutate_stillborn"></a>

### MUTATE_STILLBORN

The mutant does not build: it tests nothing.

```ts
const MUTATE_STILLBORN: i32 = 2
```

<a id="mutate_timed_out"></a>

### MUTATE_TIMED_OUT

The test ran past its time on the mutant: neither a kill nor a survival,
since a loaded machine looks the same as a hang, so it is reported apart and
too many of them refuse the run.

```ts
const MUTATE_TIMED_OUT: i32 = 3
```

<a id="mutate_build_timed_out"></a>

### MUTATE_BUILD_TIMED_OUT

The mutant's build ran past its time: it tested nothing, and too many of them refuse the run.

```ts
const MUTATE_BUILD_TIMED_OUT: i32 = 4
```

<a id="mutate_build_timeout_percent"></a>

### MUTATE_BUILD_TIMEOUT_PERCENT

The share of mutants, in percent, whose builds, or whose test runs, may run past their time before the run is refused.

```ts
const MUTATE_BUILD_TIMEOUT_PERCENT: i32 = 10
```

### mutateCode

What each character of a module's lines is, as the lexer (lexTokens) reads
the whole module: so a string, a template literal or a comment that spans
lines, or a `/*` opened mid-line, is never taken for code.

```ts
function mutateCode(text: string): Result<i32[][], string>
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the module

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;i32[][], string&gt;">

per line (splitLines), one entry per character and one more for
  the line break after it: 1 for code, 2 for a string or template text, 3
  for a comment, 0 for a space between tokens; or `Err` naming the line
  the lexer cannot read

</scalar-field>

### mutateLine

The mutants of one line of a module: each operator, literal and statement
it can change, left to right, in code only: never in a string, template
text or a comment.

```ts
function mutateLine(text: string, line: i32, kinds: i32[]): MutateMutant[]
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the line

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="line" type="i32" required>

its number, from 1

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="kinds" type="i32[]" required>

what each of its characters is, and its line break (mutateCode)

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="MutateMutant[]">

its mutants

</scalar-field>

### mutateSites

The mutants of a module's lines that a change added, inside the
declarations the contract's functions reach (scopeReach). Where code is
comes from the lexer (mutateCode), so no mutant lands in a string, a
template literal or a comment, however many lines it spans.

```ts
function mutateSites(
  text: string,
  changed: GitdiffFile,
  roots: string[],
): Result<MutateSites, string>
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the module now

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="changed" type="GitdiffFile" required>

the module's changes since the base (gitdiffChanged)

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="roots" type="string[]" required>

the contract's function names

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;MutateSites, string&gt;">

the mutants and the changed lines left out, or `Err` naming the
  line the lexer cannot read

</scalar-field>

### mutateJudge

Judges the mutants a run met.

```ts
function mutateJudge(
  r: PrReport,
  file: string,
  mutants: MutateMutant[],
  allow: AllowedSurvivor[],
  baseline: string | null,
  dropped: i32,
  outside: string,
  reached: boolean,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="r" type="PrReport" required>

the report to fill

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="file" type="string" required>

the module, from the nish root, as allowSurvivors names it

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="mutants" type="MutateMutant[]" required>

the mutants, each with its outcome

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="allow" type="AllowedSurvivor[]" required>

the survivors the contract allows

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="baseline" type="string | null" required>

why the test fails on the unmutated module, or null when it passes

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dropped" type="i32" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="outside" type="string" required>

the note on changed lines outside the tested functions
  (mutateOutsideNote), or ""

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="reached" type="boolean" required>

whether some changed line lies in code the contract's
  functions reach (MutateSites.reached), which picks the refusal when
  there is no mutant

</scalar-field>
